questions.question: The 'Statue of Unity' is located in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kevadia.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Statue of Unity is located in Kevadia, Gujarat.
 
• The Statue of Unity is the world's tallest statue, with a height of 182 meters (597 feet) which is almost double the height (including the pedestal) of the Statue of Liberty, USA.
 
• It is located on the Narmada river-facing Sardar Sarovar Dam in Kevadiya colony, Narmada District in the Indian State of Gujarat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Famous sculptor Ram V. Sutar, a Padma Bhushan Awardee is the sculptor of the Statue of Unity.
 
• India’s largest engineering and construction company Larsen & Toubro (L&T) was assigned the responsibility for designing, engineering, procurement, construction, operation and maintenance of the project.
 
• The statue was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 31 October 2018, the 143rd birth anniversary of Patel.
 
• The Statue was built in just 46 months.
 
• The previous tallest statue in India was the 41 m (135 ft) statue of Veera Abhaya Anjaneya Hanuman Swami at the Paritala Anjaneya Temple near Vijayawada in the state of Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: Which of the following monuments is NOT located in the state of Tamil Nadu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gol Gumbaz.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gol Gumbaz**, the tomb of **Mohammed Adil Shah**, Sultan of Bijapur, is located in **Bijapur, Karnataka**.
 
• It was designed by an architect named **Yaqut of Dabul**.
 
• Gumbad is a square building topped with a circular drum over which rests a majestic dome, giving the building its nomenclature.
 
• The dome of Gol Gumbad is the largest in the world.
 
• It is built of **dark grey basalt** and decorated plasterwork.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Monument
 Description
 
 

 Mahabalipuram Rathas
 
 
**Mamallapuram** or Mahabalipuram in Tamil Nadu is a temple of art, created by the Pallava rulers.

 
Built under the patronage of **Narasimhavarman I** (630-668 CE), these rathas are a group of five monolithic free-standing temples.

 
 
 

 Vivekananda Rock Memorial
 
 
**Vivekananda Rock Memorial** is a monument in **Vavathurai, Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu** at the Tri-junction of the Indian Ocean, Bay of Bengal and the Arabian sea.

 
It was built in **1970** in honour of Swami Vivekananda who is said to have attained enlightenment on the rock where he mediated in **1892**.

 
 
 

 Brihadeeswarar Temple
 
 
**Brihadeshwara Temple**, also known as **Raja Rajeswara Temple**, is dedicated to Shiva and is located in **Thanjavur (Tamil Nadu)**.

 
The temple entered the **UNESCO World Heritage Site list in 1987** and is also a part of "Great Living Chola Temples".

questions.question: In which city of Gujarat will you find the Uparkot Buddhist Caves?

__
 
• Uparkot Buddhist Caves are located in Junagadh.
 
• Uparkot caves are ancient man-made caverns.
 
• The caves are a part of the Junagadh Buddhist Cave Groups.
 
• It is situated in the eastern part of Junagadh of Gujarat. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• There are a total of 29 caves(all Buddhist).
 
• 25 caves were used as Viharas or residential caves while 4 were used as Chaitya or prayer hills.
 
 
 
• Kanheri caves are rock-cut caves related to Buddhism located in Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Maharashtra.
 
 
• These caves served as Viharas and Chaityas to the Buddhist monks.
 
 
 
• **Ellora caves **is a famous cave located in the **Sambhajinagar** (former Aurangabad) district of Maharashtra, India.

questions.question: The National Salt Satyagraha Memorial is located in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The National Salt Satyagraha Memorial is located in Dandi, **Gujarat.**
 
• Dandi March or Salt Satyagraha was started by Mahatma Gandhi in Sabarmati launched on March 12, 1930, and it lasted till April 6, 1930, in Dandi (Navsari).
 
• It was a part of Non-violent Civil Disobedience.
 
• It was against the tax collected by the British Raj on salt and Gandhi opposed this by producing salt through evaporation.
 
• This significantly influenced American activists Martin Luther King, James Bevel, and others.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• It is also known as the White Flowing River as all people took part in the march by wearing **White Khadi.**
 
• Gandhi called it the “Poor Man’s Struggle”.
 
• Due to this, mass civil disobedience was observed and Indians boycotted British clothes and goods.
 
• International Walk for Justice and Freedom – Mahatma Gandhi Foundation re-framed and cast the Salt March in 2005 on the 75th anniversary of the **Dandi March.**

questions.question: In which of the following Indian states will you find the Buxa Fort?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Buxa Fort **is located in the Buxa Tiger Reserve, in the **Kalchini CD block of the Alipurduar subdivision **of the Alipurduar district, **West Bengal,** at an elevation of 867 metres (2,844 feet).
 
• **Alipurduar, **the nearest town, is 30 kilometres (19 miles) away.
 
• The fort was utilised by the Bhutanese King to secure the section of the border between Tibet and India that passed through Bhutan.
 
• Hundreds of refugees arrived at the location afterwards, during the upheaval in Tibet's occupation, and used the abandoned fort as a haven.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buxa Tiger Reserve **is a tiger reserve and national park in northern West Bengal, India, that spans 760 square kilometres.
 
• It varies in altitude from 60 metres in the Gangetic Plains to 1,750 metres on the Himalayan border in the north.
 
• The reserve is home to at least 284 different bird species.

questions.question: Which of the following forts is located in Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mehrangarh Fort.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Mehrangarh Fort is a **1,200-acre (486-hectare) fort** located in **Jodhpur,** Rajasthan, India.
 
• It was constructed** in 1459** by **Rajput ruler Rao Jodha**, though most of the existing structure is from the **17th century.**
 
• The** chhatri of Kirat Singh Soda**, a soldier who died defending Mehrangarh, is located to the **left of the fort.**
 
• There are **seven gates**, including **Jai Pol** (which means "victory gate"), which was built by **Maharaja Man Singh** to celebrate his triumphs over the troops of **Jaipur and Bikaner in 1806.**
 
• The** Fattehpol** (also known as the "victory gate") celebrates** Maharaja Ajit Singh's** triumph over the** Mughals.**
 
• On a **vertical cliff, four hundred feet** above Jodhpur's skyline, the Mehrangarh Fort rises a hundred feet in majesty.
 
• It is also known as the **Citadel of the Sun.**
 
• Its proportions are so massive that **Rudyard Kipling **referred to it as **"the creation of giants.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sindhudurg Fort:**__

 __
 
• It is a medieval fort located on an island in the** Arabian Sea** just off the coast of **Maharashtra, India.**
 
• **Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj **constructed the fort.
 
• The fortress is located on the coast of** Malvan town** in Sindhudurg District, Maharashtra's Konkan area, **450 kilometers** south of Mumbai.
 
• The original killedars, the** Sakpal Naik family,** still live in one of the **fort's 16 houses.**
 
 
 
• **Bidar Fort**:__
 __
 
• Bidar Fort is a fort at **Bidar, Karnataka, India.**
 
• In** 1427**, **Sultan Ahmad Shah I** of the **Bahmanid Dynasty** relocated his capital from **Gulbarga to Bidar** and constructed a fort and a variety of Islamic structures.
 
• The fort of Bidar contains about **30 monuments.**
 
• In** 2014, UNESCO **added the complex to its "tentative list" of potential World Heritage Sites.
 
• The rise and fall of the Bahmani dynasty, the emergence and split of the five Deccan Sultans, capture by the Barid Shahi and Adil Shahi dynasties, and eventually being won by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb in the blockade of Bidar in 1657 have all been** **witnessed** **by the Bidar Fort.
 
 
 
• **Asigarh Fort:**__
 
 
• It is also known as** Hansi Fort**, which is a fort on the **eastern bank of Amti Lake** in Hansi, **Haryana, India.**
 
• The fort is regarded to be one of ancient **India's most impenetrable forts**, and ASI named it a** centrally protected monument in 1937**.
 
• **King Anangpal Tomar** is thought to have built the current Asigarh fort building, which was later improved by **Prithviraj Chauhan.**
 
• The fortress was regarded as the **"key to the Deccan"** because it commands a path through the** Satpuras** connecting the** Narmada and Tapti river basins**, one of the most significant routes from northern India to the Deccan.

questions.question: Sri Akal Takht Sahib is located within the _________ complex.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Golden Temple.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Akal Takht is one of five takhts ( which means "seats of power" ) of the Sikhs.**
 
• It is **located in the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar, Punjab, India.**
 
• The three Takhts are in Punjab: - 
 
 
• **Akal Takht in Amritsar.**
 
• **Sri Keshgarh Sahib in Anandpur.**
 
• **Sri Damdama Sahib at Talwandi Sabo Bhatinda district.**
 
 
 
• The other two of the five Takhts are:
 
 
• **Takht Sri Patna Sahib, Patna in Bihar.**
 
• **Takht Sri Hazoor Sahib at Nanded in Maharashtra.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **​​__Patna Sahib**​

 
 
• Takht Sri Patna Sahib** also known as Harmandir Sahib**, is a Gurdwara in Patna, Bihar, India.
 
• It was to **commemorate the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh,** the tenth Guru of the Sikhs on December 1666.
 
• It was **built by Maharaja Ranjit Singh **(1780-1839), the first Maharaja of the Sikh Empire.
 
 
 
• **Golden Temple**
 
 
• The **Harmandir Sahib, or Golden Temple,** in Amritsar, Punjab, India.
 
• The first **Harmandir Sahib was built in 1604 by Guru Arjan, the fifth Sikh Guru.**
 
• A **central religious place of the Sikhs.**
 
• It is a** symbol of human brotherhood and equality.**
 
 
 
• **Gurudwara Bangla Sahib​**
 
 
• ​Gurudwara Bangla Sahib is** situated in Delhi City.**
 
• Built in the sacred visit of Sri Guru Harikrishna Ji to Delhi.
 
 
 
• **Paonta Sahib**
 
 
• Gurudwara in Paonta Sahib is in the **district of Sirmour, Himachal Pradesh.**
 
• This Gurdwara was** built in memory of Guru Gobind Singh Ji, the tenth guru of Sikhs.**
 
• The** Dasam Granth** was **written here by Guru Gobind Singh Ji.**

questions.question: Rudreshwara, popularly known as Ramappa Temple, is located in _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Telangana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Ramappa Temple, also known as the Rudreshwara temple, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Telangana, India. 
 
• Its construction started in the year 1213 CE by Recharla Rudra, a General of Kakatiya ruler Ganapati Deva 1199–1262.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• World Heritage Sites are some of the special places present in the world which are protected by the international body UNESCO.
 
• UNESCO celebrates 'World Heritage Day' every year on 18 April to create awareness among people about these places.
 
• According to the Union Ministry of Cultural Affairs, the total number of UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India is 40.
 
• Khangchendzonga National Park is the only Mixed UNESCO site in India.​

questions.question: The Hill Palace Museum is located in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **East of Thripunithura**, on a **hillside,** is where the **Hill Palace Museum** is located.
 
• Since** 1855,** the** rulers of Cochin** have had their **official residence in this Royal Mansion.**
 
• The historical evidence suggests that** Ravi Varma**, who governed between **1853 and 1864,** constructed the **oldest building** in this royal complex.
 
• The palace complex, which consists of** 49 buildings, **displays **Kerala's traditional ancient architectural dogmas.**
 
• One needs to climb around** 200 steps** from the place entrance to reach the main door.
 
• After the passing of** Rama Varma Pareekshit Thampuran in 1964,** the Hill palace complex came under the control of the **Palace Administration Board.**
 
• The **University of Cochin** was given the palace for lease by the **Administration Board in 1972.**

questions.question: In which of the following Indian states were the remains of the ancient Vikramshila University discovered?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vikramshila** is an ancient site located 40 km away from the Bhagalpur city of Bihar.
 
• The small town is famous for housing **Vikramshila University**, which was built under the guidance of **Dharmapala, a Pala King of the 8th century AD**.
 
• Situated on top of the hills along the banks of the river Ganges, the university became a learning centre of Tantric Buddhism.
 
• Over the years, Vikramshila became one of the most popular Buddhist destinations in India and a major tourist spot in Bihar. 
 
• It prospered for about four centuries before it was destroyed by **Bakhtiyar Khilji **along with the other major centres of Buddhism in India **around** **1193**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **During the Pala Empire, Vikramashila**, along with Nalanda and Odantapuri, was one of India's three most prominent Buddhist monasteries.
 
• In response to a perceived decrease in the quality of study at Nalanda, the Pala ruler Dharmapala (783–820 AD) founded Vikramashila.
